children: Next pleasantly surprised the market with a small upgrade to full-year profit guidance driven by higher full-price sales expectations and better-than-expected cost savings, Quilter Cheviot analyst Mamta Valechha says in a note. The retailer continued its strong momentum with a pleasing earnings report with investors expecting a steady guide at this stage given the recent rise in inflation, Valechha says. "In a backdrop of a cautious U.K. consumer, it is better to own more defensive and high-quality plays within U.K. retail, and Next ticked these boxes given its exposure towards more premium fashion brands, kids wear and less exposure to a lower income consumer," Valechha says. Shares are up 1.3% at 14,740 pence and are up 11% in the year to date.(anthony.orunagoriainoff@dowjones.com)
